fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The writer says the first book covers all that Jesus began to do and to teach, "…until the day He was taken up to heaven…" (Acts 1:2). So the book runs right up to that exact day. Quite the stretch for one book.

John does show up in this passage, so I see the pull. Jesus mentions that "John baptized with water" (Acts 1:5). But the writer says the first book goes "…until the day He was taken up to heaven…" (Acts 1:2). That day is the one the book runs to.

Elders are real people in the Bible, baker, but they're not the ones here. The verse says Jesus gave His instructions to "…the apostles He had chosen." (Acts 1:2). Elders aren't in this verse at all. Only the apostles are.

Scribes are in the Bible, friend, so I get why the word came to mind. But this verse says Jesus gave instructions to "…the apostles He had chosen." (Acts 1:2). Scribes aren't mentioned in this verse. Only the apostles are.

This one is actually true, friend. The text says that after His suffering, Jesus "…presented Himself to them with many convincing proofs that He was alive." (Acts 1:3). Many, not a few. He appeared to them over a span of forty days.

Not quite, baker. Jesus says, "…in a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit." (Acts 1:5). A few days is not many years. I'd never leave a batch in the oven for years, and Jesus isn't leaving them waiting that long either.

You got it, baker. They ask, "Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" (Acts 1:6). The passage says earlier that Jesus spoke about the kingdom of God (Acts 1:3). I respect a baker who just asks.

That's right, baker. Jesus says, "It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority." (Acts 1:7). The Father fixed them, and they're not the apostles' to know. I think that's a relief, honestly.
Guards is a fun guess, friend, but not what Jesus says. He tells them, "…you will be My witnesses…" (Acts 1:8). Standing watch isn't the job He names. He calls them witnesses.

That's it, baker. Jesus says they'll be His witnesses "…in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth." (Acts 1:8). It starts with Jerusalem and goes all the way out. That's a long list, and the last item is HUGE.

You've got it, baker. The two men say, "This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven." (Acts 1:11). That's why my ovens stay ready. As for when, Jesus says no one knows the day or the hour except the Father (Matthew 24:36).

Not what they said, friend. The two men say, "This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven." (Acts 1:11). They tell the apostles He will come back. That's the word they give.
